title: L1: Numbers in Binary
description: 4-bit binary conversion through worked examples and practice.

steps.title: The 4 Columns
steps.content:
4-bit binary

Binary uses four columns. Each column has a value. A 1 means add that column. A 0 means skip it.

8421
1011

Column 8 is on. Column 4 is off. Columns 2 and 1 are on. So: 8 + 2 + 1 = 11.

Now try these. Each one only has a single 1.
steps.js: BinaryLesson.createPractice({containerId:'y8bin-intro',questions:[{prompt:'What is this worth?',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([0,0,0,1],[8,4,2,1]),answer:'1',right:'Correct. Only the 1 column is on.'},{prompt:'What is this worth?',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([0,0,1,0],[8,4,2,1]),answer:'2',right:'Correct. Only the 2 column is on.'},{prompt:'What is this worth?',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([0,1,0,0],[8,4,2,1]),answer:'4',right:'Correct. Only the 4 column is on.'},{prompt:'What is this worth?',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([1,0,0,0],[8,4,2,1]),answer:'8',right:'Correct. Only the 8 column is on.'}]});

steps.title: Step Through: 1010 to Denary
steps.content:
Step through: binary to denary

Now two columns are on at the same time. Click through to see how it works.
steps.js:
BinaryLesson.createStepper({containerId:'y8bin-s1',steps:[{title:'The binary number is 1010',html:'
1010
',note:'Orange digits are 1s. Grey digits are 0s. Only the 1s add to the total.'},{title:'Put each bit under its column',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([1,0,1,0],[8,4,2,1]),note:'Column 8 is on. Column 4 is off. Column 2 is on. Column 1 is off.'},{title:'Add only the columns that are on',html:'

8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10

',note:'Cross out the 0 columns. Add the rest. 8 + 2 = 10.'}]});

steps.title: Step Through: 1101 to Denary
steps.content:
Step through: three columns on

This time three columns are on and one is off.
steps.js:
BinaryLesson.createStepper({containerId:'y8bin-s2',steps:[{title:'The binary number is 1101',html:'
1101
',note:'Three orange digits, one grey digit. Three columns will be added.'},{title:'Put each bit under its column',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([1,1,0,1],[8,4,2,1]),note:'Columns 8, 4 and 1 are on. Column 2 is off.'},{title:'Add only the columns that are on',html:'

8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 13

',note:'Cross out column 2. Add the rest. 8 + 4 + 1 = 13.'}]});

steps.title: Step Through: 0110 to Denary
steps.content:
Step through: starting with a 0

A 0 in the first position just means the 8 column is off. Nothing unusual about it.
steps.js:
BinaryLesson.createStepper({containerId:'y8bin-s3',steps:[{title:'The binary number is 0110',html:'
0110
',note:'Two middle digits are orange. First and last are grey.'},{title:'Put each bit under its column',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([0,1,1,0],[8,4,2,1]),note:'Only columns 4 and 2 are on.'},{title:'Add only the columns that are on',html:'

8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 6

',note:'Cross out columns 8 and 1. Add the rest. 4 + 2 = 6.'}]});

steps.title: Practice: Binary to Denary
steps.content:
Practice: binary to denary

Find which columns are on, add them up, and type the total.

steps.title: Step Through: Convert 9 to Binary
steps.content:
Step through: denary to binary

Going the other way: choose which columns add up to the denary number. A column that is used gets a 1. A column that is not used gets a 0.
steps.js:
BinaryLesson.createStepper({containerId:'y8bin-s4',steps:[{title:'The denary number is 9',html:'
9
',note:'Use the same four columns: 8, 4, 2, 1. We need columns that add to 9.'},{title:'Start with column 8',html:'

8 + ? = 9

',note:'Column 8 is on. We have 1 more to make.'},{title:'Choose the rest of the columns',html:'

8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 9

',note:'Columns 8 and 1 are on. Columns 4 and 2 are off.'},{title:'Write the bits under the columns',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([1,0,0,1],[8,4,2,1]),note:'On columns get 1. Off columns get 0. So 9 in binary is 1001.'}]});

steps.title: Step Through: Convert 14 to Binary
steps.content:
Step through: three columns on

This time three columns are on and one is off.
steps.js:

14

8 + ? = 14

',note:'Column 8 is on. We have 6 more to make.'},{title:'Choose the rest of the columns',html:'

8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 14

',note:'Columns 8, 4 and 2 are on. Column 1 is off.'},{title:'Write the bits under the columns',html:BinaryLesson.bitTable([1,1,1,0],[8,4,2,1]),note:'On columns get 1. Off columns get 0. So 14 in binary is 1110.'}]});

steps.title: Practice: Denary to Binary
steps.content:
Practice: denary to binary

Choose columns that add to the number. Always write four digits, using a 0 when a column is off.
steps.js: BinaryLesson.createPractice({containerId:'y8bin-pb',questions:[{prompt:'Convert 1 to 4-bit binary.',answer:'0001',right:'Correct. Only column 1 is on. 0001.'},{prompt:'Convert 4 to 4-bit binary.',answer:'0100',right:'Correct. Only column 4 is on. 0100.'},{prompt:'Convert 6 to 4-bit binary.',answer:'0110',right:'Correct. 4 + 2 = 6. So 0110.'},{prompt:'Convert 11 to 4-bit binary.',answer:'1011',right:'Correct. 8 + 2 + 1 = 11. So 1011.'},{prompt:'Convert 3 to 4-bit binary.',answer:'0011',right:'Correct. 2 + 1 = 3. So 0011.'},{prompt:'Convert 15 to 4-bit binary.',answer:'1111',right:'Correct. All four columns are on: 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 15. So 1111.'},{prompt:'Convert 12 to 4-bit binary.',answer:'1100',right:'Correct. 8 + 4 = 12. So 1100.'}]});

steps.content:

Both directions, five questions picked at random. Get them all right to move on.
